summary: Corpus extraction artifacts found during quarantine review (Dhammapada footnotes, Kalevala front-matter/title-clipping, Mabinogion footnote bleed, OCR typos, one thin chunk)
description:
Same apparatus-leak family as todo:50438e23 (Mead/Waite/Bellows/Charles/Taylor editions), surfaced this time by the qwen-3-4b-guru quarantine review passes (2026-08-05/06) rather than the edge review. New instances, not yet in that ticket's scope:

- Dhammapada: a large fraction of chunks are 50-80% Max Muller translator footnotes rather than verse text (tag-bait — the footnote prose draws its own spurious tag proposals).
- Kalevala: chunk 144 leaks Book II front-matter into the body; chunk 271 concatenates the glossary into the preceding chunk (chunker overran); rune/canto titles get clipped at some chunk starts.
- Mabinogion: chunks 190 and 191 have footnote bleed into the body, same class as the Dhammapada issue.
- Jowett and W.F. Crawford editions have scattered OCR typos (not systematic apparatus, just transcription noise — lower priority, may not be worth a dedicated pass).
- mooney.137 is a thin chunk (very little content), flagged in passing, not yet characterized further.

None of these were root-caused to specific chunk.py patterns the way todo:50438e23's Mead/Waite cases were — that diagnostic work is still needed per source before a fix can land.
